clue.text: Autumn is on the turn — that's a bit of luck

indicators.note: on here means added to the end of the other piece, so the season follows the turning

parts.note: to turn something, such as a handle, is to wind it
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: The season is changing, and that happens to be fortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' reads as one idiom for a season changing, but it splits: 'on' is a placement word and 'turn' is a verb for rotating a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unexpected piece of good fortune, originally fruit blown down from a tree.

clue.text: Lawless US area of old in a stew?

parts.note: stew is the compass point WEST with its letters disordered, which a clue could signal with the word wild

explanation.surface: A rowdy part of old America finds itself in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer, read as a cryptic instruction, would itself produce 'stew'. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical name for the American frontier in its unruly nineteenth-century days of outlaws and gunfights.

clue.text: Exalted Russian actor able to afford sea passage

indicators.note: exalted means raised up, so in a down entry the name is written upwards

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A celebrated Russian performer has enough money for a ticket on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exalted' lifts IVAN upwards to give NAVI. 'Afford' in the definition means provide, not pay for: water that offers ships a way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes water deep and wide enough for ships to travel through, so it provides a route.

clue.text: Makes for woman of enigmatic style

parts.note: taken as written
Ms is the title (style) for a woman that keeps her marital status unknown

explanation.surface: A dressmaker produces clothes for a lady whose fashion sense is hard to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' here means a form of address, not fashion: the title that does not say whether a woman is married.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: someone who shapes or creates a thing constructs it.

clue.text: Strike finally engulfs businessman

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: finally means last, as in arriving last
an MBA is a holder of the business degree Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Industrial action at last overwhelms a company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action but means hit, and 'engulfs' is the containment signal. The businessman is known by his degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to beat or thrash someone, also to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: Cut the drink

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to score or gash, as in Shakespeare's snake that was only wounded

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an archaic verb for gashing or scoring something, and whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Letter of reference

definitions.meaning: a written symbol such as a letter of the alphabet
an old term for a testimonial given by an employer about a servant or worker

explanation.surface: A written testimonial for someone seeking a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole reads as one phrase for a testimonial, but it splits at 'of' into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a printed or written symbol, and a testimonial vouching for somebody's conduct.

clue.text: Stupid, like thieves

definitions.meaning: from the saying about people who are very close friends being as close as thieves

explanation.surface: Dim, in the way that burglars are.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: informal for slow-witted, and the idiom describing people as intimate as thieves.

clue.text: Tomboy's Orkney retreat

parts.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney Islands, off the north of Scotland
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A boyish girl has a hideaway in the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: HOY is one of the Orkney Islands, off northern Scotland, known for its sea stack the Old Man of Hoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old word for a boisterous, high-spirited girl.

clue.text: Devilish opponent capturing rook achieves mate

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a fiend is a devil, an evil enemy
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A fiendishly clever chess player takes a rook and delivers checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess scene hides the definition: 'mate' is a pal, not checkmate. 'Capturing' puts R inside FIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in British informal speech: a pal or companion.

clue.text: Swain can get nothing right

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis

explanation.surface: A young suitor is unable to do a single thing correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can get' simply says the definition can acquire the two pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old poetic word for a young male suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: Seeing point finally in ethics, that's the human condition

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter goes inside the word for ethics

parts.note: ethics is the study or practice of morality

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: At last grasping the purpose of moral philosophy: it is simply what being human is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts T, taken by 'finally' from 'point', inside MORALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being subject to death is the state every human shares.

clue.text: Downtrodden worker carries on with wash

parts.note: to wage a war or campaign is to carry it on
lave is a literary verb meaning to wash

explanation.surface: An exploited employee keeps going with the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries on' looks like persevering, but it is the verb used of conducting a war or campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone wholly dependent on pay from drudging employment, with little freedom.

clue.text: An antlered creature's backbone

indicators.note: back, the first half of the last word, tells us the animal's name is written backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer with antlers

explanation.surface: The spine of a stag or similar animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word must be split in two: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'bone' alone is the definition, loosely, since the answer is a joint made of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose example: the joint where leg meets foot, popularly thought of as a bony part.

clue.text: Prepare to print the rest, in case

indicators.note: in tells us the resting place sits inside the word for a case

parts.note: a suit is a case brought in a court of law
bed is where one takes rest, and a word for rest itself

explanation.surface: Get the remaining pages ready for the press, just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' is not the idiom meaning as a precaution: 'in' is the containment signal and 'case' is a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper job: checking and correcting copy before it goes to press.

clue.text: To ruin a single good person is immoral

parts.note: to dish someone's chances is British informal for to ruin them
a single is one
St is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Destroying even one decent human being is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH as a verb is British informal for ruin or spoil, as in dishing someone's hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of lacking integrity or principle.

clue.text: Leaves untouched in the clay, perhaps

definitions.text: Leaves untouched in the clay, perhaps

parts.words: Leaves untouched in the clay, perhaps
parts.note: the leaves are tobacco and the clay is a clay pipe: what stays unburnt in the bowl after a smoke

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests foliage lying undisturbed in soil. The leaves are tobacco, and 'the clay' is a clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The plug of unburnt tobacco remaining at the bottom of a pipe bowl after smoking.

clue.text: Cartoonist was careful about being vulgar

parts.note: David Low was a famous British political cartoonist, creator of Colonel Blimp
to mind something is to be careful about it, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: An artist of comic drawings took pains not to be coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir David Low drew political cartoons for British newspapers from the 1920s to the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having coarse tastes or thoughts.

clue.text: Stress name is not to be placed below

indicators.note: is not says the letter for name is absent from the word for stress

parts.note: to underline a point is to stress it

explanation.surface: An instruction that the word stress should not be written at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is not' removes N from UNDERLINE. UNDERLINE has two Ns; the second goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie beneath something, literally or as its foundation.

clue.text: Each child is individual

parts.note: per means for each, as in ten pounds per head
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Every boy and girl is unique.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a single human being.

clue.text: Country with no alternative to the socialist path?

parts.note: taken as written
the socialist side is the left, and its alternative is the right, abbreviated R
a way is a path or route

explanation.surface: A nation where the left-wing road is the only option.
explanation.walkthrough: The socialist side in politics is the left, so its alternative is the right, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: Casually add one name to end of cast

indicators.note: to end of says the two short pieces are attached after the word for cast

parts.note: to cast is to throw, as with a fishing line
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Without fuss, put one more actor on the bottom of the list of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a list of actors but is the verb for hurling. 'To end of' puts I and N after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to include something extra in an offhand manner, such as a remark.

clue.text: Puzzle a poacher

definitions.meaning: informal for a tricky problem that teases the brain
poachers catch trout by stroking their bellies with the fingers, known as tickling

explanation.surface: Baffle someone who takes game illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' reads as a verb but is a noun. Catching trout by hand by stroking the belly is called tickling.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a teasing problem, and one who catches trout by hand illegally.

clue.text: Visit off-colour Indian?

parts.note: someone off-colour is below par, so in this down entry the other piece sits below the letters PAR
to visit someone is to see them, as in see a doctor

explanation.surface: Call on a poorly man from India.
explanation.walkthrough: A positional joke: 'off-colour' means below par, so in this down entry SEE (visit) is written below PAR. The question mark marks the answer as one example of an Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the Zoroastrian community of India, descended from Persians.

clue.text: Texans remember it as not quite fashionable

indicators.note: not quite says the word for fashionable falls short, losing its ending

parts.note: a la mode is a French phrase used in English for fashionable

explanation.surface: People in Texas recall something as being a little out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts DE from A LA MODE. 'Remember the Alamo' was the Texan battle cry after the 1836 siege of that mission.
explanation.definitionFit: The mission in San Antonio whose siege gave Texas its famous battle cry.

clue.text: Float freely up

indicators.note: freely says the letters of the word before it move about without restraint

explanation.surface: Drift without restraint into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adverb: high in the air or overhead.

clue.text: Would he tear up a beer-chit?

definitions.text: Would he tear up a beer-chit?

indicators.note: tearing something up breaks it into pieces, so the letters after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who might well rip a voucher for ale to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'tear up' rearranges A BEER-CHIT, and a member of this teetotal society would refuse a voucher for ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a temperance society pledged to total abstinence from alcohol, named after a biblical clan.

clue.text: A mountain has lost its foot

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot of a word is its bottom letter, which is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A peak whose lower slopes have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' is the whole definition: the Greek name for that letter. 'Lost its foot' drops S from HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter corresponding to the first letter of our alphabet.

clue.text: Be obstructive — there's nothing original in that

indicators.note: in tells us the two pieces go inside the word that 'that' stands for

parts.note: that points back to the opening phrase: to be obstructive is to stall
O looks like zero, nothing
something original is new

explanation.surface: Stop blocking things; the tactic is hardly a fresh idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' refers back to the definition and stands for STALL, another word for it; 'in' puts O and NEW inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to block progress by refusing to cooperate or answer, from cricket's defensive batting.

clue.text: Ride bike for exercise and take pulse

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise lessons at school
dal is the Indian name for split lentils, a pulse

explanation.surface: Go cycling to keep fit and then measure your heart rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat but an edible seed: DAL, the lentil dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to cycle by pushing the foot levers round.

clue.text: Property of French art gallery

parts.note: art is the old form of are (thou art); the French for it is es (tu es)
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Something belonging to a museum of paintings from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art', which in French is 'tu es'. The TATE is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: land or possessions that somebody owns.

clue.text: Paper to cease publication? It's fine stuff

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a party or group
a newspaper that stops appearing is said to die

explanation.surface: Is a newspaper about to close down? It was excellent material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is the old word for cloth, so 'fine stuff' is delicate fabric, not good writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiff, translucent cotton fabric; delicate cloth.
